annotations.text:
Four layout directions for the SQL client, same tokens as the component kit (Geist, dark neutral, one blue accent), same sample query and data in each so only the structure differs.
Pick one; we build that into the app and drop the rest.

A · Classic three-pane
Why: zero learning curve, schema always visible, results under the editor like every SQL tool people already know.
Tradeoff: three fixed panes eat height on a laptop; results get ~300px.

B · Notebook cells
Why: each query keeps its own result next to it, so exploratory work reads top to bottom and the file becomes a record of the session. Side zone collapses to an icon rail.
Tradeoff: less natural for one big query edited repeatedly; wide result sets are cramped in a 960px column.

C · Side-by-side split
Why: results get full height, so wide tables and long outputs are readable; multiple runs sit as tabs for comparing.
Tradeoff: editor is only ~600px wide; long SQL lines wrap or scroll.

D · Focus + command palette
Why: the most minimal. Editor owns the screen; schema, files and connections live behind ⌘K; results slide up as a sheet only when needed.
Tradeoff: schema browsing is hidden behind a keystroke, which some teammates will miss coming from pgAdmin.
